steps.title: The pattern
say: With competing consumers, several identical workers read one queue, and each message goes to one of them. So adding workers adds capacity.
This tour takes about ten minutes. Each step tells you what to do, waits while you do it, and then explains what you see. Press Continue when you are ready.

steps.title: The confirmation emails
say: This is a shop. Every order needs a confirmation email, and at busy times one worker cannot send them fast enough.

So the jobs go on one shared queue, and several identical workers take from it. The broker gives each job to one worker. Checkout publishes six orders a second. Two workers start with Play. A third is waiting for you to start it.

steps.title: Run it
steps.do: Press Play, at the top of the page under Run it.

expect.note: Not everything is running yet. Play takes a few seconds.

say: Press Play. It creates the shared queue, starts Worker 1 and Worker 2, and then Checkout.
Press Continue when the dots on the diagram are moving.

steps.title: One of the workers
steps.do: Click logs on the Worker 1 node.

expect.note: The Worker 1 log is not open yet.

say: Click logs on the Worker 1 node. It sends one email at a time, and each takes a little under half a second. Worker 2 runs the same code and takes different jobs.

steps.title: Not keeping up
steps.do: Watch the number on the queue inside the broker for ten seconds.
say: Watch the number on the queue in the broker. It is climbing. Two workers send about five emails a second between them, and Checkout confirms six orders a second. The backlog grows.

expect.note: The apps are not all running. Press Play first.

steps.title: Add a worker
steps.do: Click the Worker 3 node, and press Start in the panel that opens.
say: Now add capacity. Click the Worker 3 node, and press Start in the panel that opens.
Nothing else changes. Worker 3 runs the same code, binds the same queue, and the broker starts sharing the jobs between three.

steps.title: The backlog turns round
steps.do: Watch the number on the queue again.
say: Watch the number on the queue again. With three workers, emails go out faster than orders come in, and the backlog drains. That is the whole pattern: more workers, more capacity, with no change to the publisher or to the other workers.

steps.title: Crash a worker
steps.do: Open the card A worker crashes, and press Break it.

expect.note: The card is not in effect yet. Open it and press Break it.

say: Now break it. Scroll to Break it, open the card called A worker crashes, and press Break it.
One of the workers is killed while it holds jobs it has taken but not finished.

steps.title: Its jobs go to the others
steps.do: Read the other worker's log beside the diagram.
say: The log beside the diagram belongs to another worker. Within a moment it sends the jobs the crashed worker was holding, marked redelivered. There are at most five, the queue's limit for each worker.

Nothing is lost, and every other job keeps flowing, only more slowly. One caution: a worker that crashed after sending an email and before acknowledging the job leaves that job to be sent again. It is one worker per delivery, not one email per order.

expect.note: The card is not in effect, so there is nothing to see yet.

steps.title: Start it again
steps.do: Press Reset, in the bar at the top of the page.

expect.note: The workers are not all back yet. Press Reset in the bar at the top.

say: Press Reset. The crashed worker starts again and takes a share straight away. On a shared queue there is no standby.

steps.title: Freeze a worker
steps.do: Open the card A worker hangs, and the others carry on, and press Break it.

expect.note: The card is not in effect yet. Open it and press Break it.

say: Now a worker that hangs. Open the card called A worker hangs, and the others carry on, and press Break it.
One worker freezes. It stays connected, but stops sending emails and stops acknowledging.

steps.title: Only its own jobs are stuck
steps.do: Read the other worker's log beside the diagram, and look at the worker nodes.
say: The other workers keep sending. Only the frozen worker's own jobs are stuck: the five it took before it froze. In the diagram it reads: active, not acking, and it gets no more jobs.
Compare the Exclusive Consumer pattern, where a hung consumer stops everything. Here the broker passes over a worker that is full, and gives the next job to one with room.

expect.note: The card is not in effect, so there is nothing to see yet.

steps.title: Stop the frozen worker
steps.do: Press Reset, in the bar at the top of the page.

expect.note: The workers are not all back yet. Reset takes a few seconds here.

say: Press Reset. The frozen worker is stopped, as a health check would do, and after five seconds it is killed. Its five jobs go to another worker, marked redelivered, and it is started again.

steps.title: When to use it
say: That is competing consumers. Use it when work items are independent and the load varies.
The cost is that there is no order across workers, and a crashed worker's unacknowledged jobs go to the others, so a job can be done twice.
Press Cleanup when you are done, or pick another pattern from the sidebar.
